name: Greccio the Song, a sacred musical inspired by the life of St Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio
venue: 15 Dufferin Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Greccio: The Song
A sacred musical inspired by the life of Saint Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio.
Saturday, 5 December 2026 at 7:30 PM
Venue: Allan Gibbs Centre, Wellington College, 15 Dufferin StreetMount Victoria, Wellington.

Step into the story of Saint Francis of Assisi, whose longing to contemplate the humility and wonder of Christ’s birth led to the first living Nativity at Greccio in 1223. Greccio: The Song is a community faith-and-arts production bringing together live music, choir, drama, movement, and sacred storytelling in a celebration of faith, family, peace, and renewal. At the heart of the musical is Francis’ desire to make the mystery of Christmas visible and tangible: “We wish to see the Child as He was in Bethlehem.” — St Francis of Assisi.

Through music and dramatic scenes, the production follows Francis’ journey of conversion, simplicity, service, and love of Christ, culminating in the Christmas night at Greccio. The musical features music by Douglas Mews, Dr Robert Loretz, and Franciscan friars from the Philippines, with Artistic/Creative Direction by Dave Cecilio.

Presented by Vineyard House — A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family, Greccio: The Song is also part of a special year of commemoration, marking the Jubilee Year of Saint Francis of Assisi (1226–2026) and recognising 60 years of diplomatic relations between New Zealand and the Philippines.

About the production

Greccio: The Song has been created as a community faith and arts initiative, bringing together volunteer actors, musicians, singers, dancers and supporters from across Wellington. It is an invitation to encounter Christmas through the eyes of Saint Francis — not simply as a familiar story, but as a living mystery of humility, joy, peace and love.

Come and let your hearts be renewed.

Presented by: Vineyard House, A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family

Website: www.marriageandfamily.org.nz⁠

Enquiries: vineyardhouse.nz@gmail.com

name: Taha Hotu in person hui Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Wellington
venue: Massey University, Block 1 Te Whare Pukākā, Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Come along to the Taha Hotu Deaf and Disabled Artists Initiative Wellington Hui. Tuesday 8 December 1pm-3:30pm. Ahumairangi Studios, College of Creative Arts, Massey University.


Hui Information:

Deaf and disabled artists, arts workers and creative practitioners are invited to join this low-key disabled led hui at Ahumairangi Studios. The hui will be led by Stace Robertson, Lead Accessibility Advisor at Arts Access Aotearoa.

The hui is an opportunity to connect as Deaf and disabled artists and arts workers, share our goals, ask questions, share crip hacks and learn from each other. There will be time to share arts practice and kōrero about all things disability arts.

We'll break for a light afternoon tea and there will be plenty of time to chat.

There is no cost to register for the hui.


Who can come?

We welcome any Deaf or disabled people, including neurodivergent folk and people with lived experience of mental distress who make art of any kind or who work in the arts sector.

You don’t have to be a well-known artist or have shown your work. We would love to welcome you.

If you think this might be a space for you, or you aren’t sure or would like to know more about who can come please email tahahotu@artsaccess.org.nz

long_description:
CLUEDUNNIT

DINNER WITH 'MURDER ON THE MENU'

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. From the moment you arrive, you'll be immersed in a world of drama, laughter, and unexpected twists.

Whether you're planning a unique night out with friends, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying an unforgettable evening with colleagues, Cluedunnit at InterContinental Wellington promises the perfect blend of fine dining, mystery, and entertainment.

Guests will interact with a live cast of characters, uncover clues, and work together to crack the case, all while enjoying a delicious three-course dinner.

But beware, all is not as it seems. As secrets unravel and tensions rise, you'll need to decipher the clues, question the suspects, and piece together the evidence before it's too late. After all, where there's a will, there's a murder.

Where there's a mystery, there's a motive. Where there's a motive, there's a murder. The question is: whodunnit?

MURDER AT THE MANOR - The Story So Far...

It is 1929 and this English Cotswold beauty spot is celebrating the life of elderly heiress Rose Stimper, who, in an act of philanthropy, has bequeathed the village a large sum of money and left instructions that the villagers must decide how best to spend it. 

This will be a party like no other. Everyone has ideas on how to spend the money, and the entire village turns out to attend Pokeingham Hall, which has been thrown open for the first time in many years to host the event.

But beware, all is not as it seems. There are dark forces at work.

Enjoy a delicious three course dinner as you question the suspects, decipher the clues and work to crack the case. And please remember - where there’s a will, there’s a murder!


DINNER MENU:

STARTER: gf/v

Sashimi cut Akaroa salmon and yellow fin tuna, preserved lemon, harissa, coriander

MAIN COURSE: gf/v

Corn fed Chicken supreme, truffled portobello plin ravioli, ajo blanco, spring asparagus, chardonnay jus

VEGETARIAN MAIN COURSE: gf/df

Risotto prima vera Aged Acquerello rice, asparagus, green beans, peas, parmesan fondue

DESSERT: gf/v

Dark blood chocolate mousse, with raspberry and dark chocolate crumble.

We cater for all dietary requirements - please select the relevant option at checkout. 

BOOKING YOUR PLACE AT A TABLE: 

You will be seated around tables of 10. If it is likely that friends will be coming along too, it is best to book all your places at the same time to ensure you are all on the same table.

Please note, ticket sales will end 72 hours before the event.

www.cluedunnit.com.au

info@cluedunnit.com.au

cluedunnitwellington@ihg.com 




0450 511 945

long_description:
Join us outside the ANZ bank on Lambton Quay to call on the ANZ bank to Protect the Denniston Palteau by withdrawing support for Bathurst Resources.

Bathurst Resources has relodged their application to mine the Denniston Plateau, threatening numerous rare, threatened species of flora and fauna, some found nowhere else in the world.

We are in the midst of a climate catastrophe. By 270 on current policies and predicted growth, we will hit 3 degrees of warming creating billions of climate refugees and billions of deaths.

Stand with us to say no to profit over planet.

You are also welcome to join us prior to the main event, from 11am for chalking outside Bathurst Resouces Building, 1 Williston Street.

long_description:
Wrap a cake, share a story, and celebrate Vietnamese traditions together!

Tết is more than just a celebration. It is a time for family, connection, and passing down traditions from one generation to the next.

Join Viet Hub NZ for a hands-on Vietnamese New Year rice cake workshop, where we explore the cultural significance of traditional Tết foods and learn the art of wrapping Vietnamese rice cakes.

In collaboration with Yung Nguyen, this workshop brings our community together to celebrate Vietnamese heritage through food, storytelling, and shared experiences.

🌸 What will we explore?

Discover three traditional Vietnamese rice cakes:

🍃 Bánh Chưng – A traditional square sticky rice cake, symbolising the Earth and representing gratitude to our ancestors.

🍃 Bánh Tét – A cylindrical sticky rice cake especially popular in Southern Vietnam, traditionally enjoyed during Lunar New Year.

🍃 Bánh Ú – A pyramid-shaped sticky rice cake wrapped in leaves, reflecting the diversity of Vietnamese culinary traditions.

During the workshop, participants will have the opportunity to:

Learn about the history and cultural significance of Vietnamese rice cakes.

Explore traditional ingredients and wrapping techniques.

Experience hands-on rice cake preparation with guidance from our facilitator.

Connect with others and share memories of Tết celebrations.

Help preserve and pass on Vietnamese food traditions to the next generation.

No previous cooking experience is required. Everyone is welcome, whether you grew up celebrating Tết or are discovering Vietnamese culture for the first time.

📅 Event Details

Date: Saturday, 16 January 2027

Venue: Te Mako Naenae Community Centre, Lower Hutt

Facilitator: Yung Nguyen

Organised by: Viet Hub NZ

For many Vietnamese families living overseas, the smell of sticky rice, the sound of leaves being folded, and the joy of preparing food together bring back cherished memories of home.

Through our Viet Cuisine programme, we hope to create a welcoming space where generations and cultures come together to learn, connect, and keep these traditions alive.

Spaces are limited. Register now to join us in welcoming Tết 2027!

Uplifting Culture. Creating Opportunity. Empowering People. Together.

Viet Hub NZ | Registered Charity CC64272

name: FLINT Wellington: Get to Know a CxO
venue: level 6/44 Bowen Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

James Fuller, Co-Founder at HNRY

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.




	

James Fuller; Co-founder at HNRY

	

James Fuller began his career as an application developer, before moving into technology strategy and consultancy. After senior roles at Thomson Reuters and Deloitte, he decided to strike out on his own as a growth consultant for startup, corporate, and government clients.

It was rewarding work, but James found himself struggling with the amount of tax and financial admin involved in being self-employed. To solve the issue, he and co-founder Claire created a simple, homemade system to automate calculating and paying self-employed taxes.

They shared their system with self-employed friends, realised that there was a market for it, and got to work improving their solution .In 2017, James and Claire officially launched Hnry; a service designed to automatically calculate, pay, and file taxes for sole traders.

Today, Hnry is New Zealand’s largest, and Australasia’s fastest-growing accounting service. We process billions of dollars worth of payments every year, handling around 1% of New Zealand’s tax revenue.

Best of all, we free up thousands of hours for clients to focus more on what they do best - their jobs. Hnry is on a mission to make self-employment simple, affordable, and accessible for anyone.

id: embroidery with beads - jules + the wildflowers craft club-Colombo St & Rintoul St, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: embroidery with beads - jules + the wildflowers craft club
venue: Colombo St & Rintoul St, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
embroidery with beads workshop: Slow Down. Make something.

Join me for a cozy, beginner-friendly embroidery workshop designed for adults who want to learn something new and enjoy a creative evening together.

In this 2hour session, I’ll guide you through the basic stitches you need to get started with hand embroidery and help you start your own project on your item of clothing.

We’ll begin by practicing on small fabric squares so you can build confidence and get comfortable with your needle and thread, practice how to attach beads before starting a project onto a piece of clothing you’ve brought along or a piece of fabric from my stash — turning it into something beautifully personal and unique.

This workshop is all about slowing down, crafting together, and enjoying the process in a relaxed, welcoming space.

All materials are provided, and you’ll head home with:

A piece of practice fabric + a blank square for your next project

An embroidery hoop, needle, some thread and the fabric you need to finish your project



Soft drinks (hot and cold) and snacks will also be available to keep our creative energy flowing.

No experience is needed — just bring an item of clothing you’d love to transform (or a bag, a pouch, anything you can stitch on) and a willingness to try something new. I can’t wait to stitch with you 🤍

Please note, the workshop will be cancelled if less than 3 participants are signed up 7 days prior to the date.

AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Advanced

The Advanced workshop is for musicians who already have some experience with improvisation and jazz playing, or players with more advanced technique looking to dive deeper into the language of jazz.

Participants will take an in-depth look at playing jazz standards with the rhythm section, explore different styles and traditions, develop listening skills, and gain musical insights from the professional musicians leading the workshop.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

Christmas Fantasia

Saturday 5 December, 7pm

General admission $35 (early bird price $30 until midnight 29 Nov)

Concession $30 (early bird concession price $27 until midnight 29 Nov)

Nota Bene presents: Christmas Fantasia

From centuries-old texts to traditional carols given new musical life, this concert explores the many ways composers across different eras and cultures have interpreted the Christmas story.

Our programme brings together music from England to Appalachia, with works by Vaughan Williams, Warlock, Dalglish and Ešenvalds. The music ranges from reflective settings and rich harmonies to folk-inspired carols and familiar Christmas melodies.

Vaughan Williams’ Fantasia on Christmas Carols weaves together traditional English carol melodies, some emerging in the choir and others in the accompaniment. In contrast, Malcolm Dalglish’s Star in the East sets three Appalachian Christmas songs for choir and harp, drawing on a different folk tradition.

Joined by baritone Joe Haddow, harpist Michelle Velvin and organist Rachel Malcolm-Swindells, Nota Bene presents a programme that moves between familiar carols and less familiar musical settings.

And what better way to finish than by singing some favourite Christmas carols together? As is our tradition, we hope you’ll stay and join us for refreshments after the concert.

Rachel Malcolm-Swindells - Organ

Michelle Velvin - Harp

Joe Haddow - Baritone

name: MATRESCENCE Development Showing
venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, Nueva Zelanda
long_description:
MATRESCENCE

A development showing at Hannah Playhouse

A solo show about the collision of early motherhood, migration and art making.

A mother tries to care for her baby. An artist tries to make a show.

MATRESCENCE follows Ella (“she” in Spanish), a migrant theatremaker and new mother trying to remain creatively alive while navigating the demands, exhaustion and disorientation of early motherhood.

Part testimonial, part creative crisis and part documentary, MATRESCENCE is an anti-biography that moves between Ella’s intimate experience of postpartum life and her attempt to make theatre from inside it. She reaches out to other migrant mothers and theatremakers, searching for answers about care, identity, creativity and belonging. But the more stories she gathers, the less this seems to be a story about one woman.

Join us for a special development showing of MATRESCENCE at Hannah Playhouse, a glimpse into the making of this new documentary theatre work. This is an opportunity to experience the work in progress and be part of its creative journey.

Following the showing, we invite you to stay for an informal Q&A - audience conversation. We would love to hear your thoughts, reflections and responses to the work, while opening up a wider conversation about postpartum, care work, and the complexities of motherhood, particularly when home, family and support networks are far away.

The work is informed by research into matrescence, migration and caregiving, interviews, as well as anonymous testimonies from migrant mothers living in Aotearoa.

Please note: This is a work in development showing, not a finished production. Your presence, thoughts and feedback are warmly welcomed and will contribute to the ongoing development of MATRESCENCE.

CREATIVE TEAM

Created and performed by Romina Meneses

Directed by Mel Dodge

Production Managment: Jessie Rochford-Barber

Lights and AV design: Janis Cheng

Sound Design: Alex Quinn

Set and Costume Design: Miho Aragane

Along the way, encounter remarkable marine creatures, discover remote underwater environments and experience the thrill of ocean adventure through the eyes of those who know it best.
The Ocean Film Festival World Tour is a celebration of our oceans in all their beauty, diversity and power.
Inspiring, entertaining and thought-provoking, it’s an unforgettable experience that will leave you with a deeper appreciation for the incredible marine environments that connect us all.

name: FLINT Wellington: Get to Know a CxO
venue: level 6/44 Bowen Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

James Fuller, Co-Founder at HNRY

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.




	

James Fuller; Co-founder at HNRY

	

James Fuller began his career as an application developer, before moving into technology strategy and consultancy. After senior roles at Thomson Reuters and Deloitte, he decided to strike out on his own as a growth consultant for startup, corporate, and government clients.

It was rewarding work, but James found himself struggling with the amount of tax and financial admin involved in being self-employed. To solve the issue, he and co-founder Claire created a simple, homemade system to automate calculating and paying self-employed taxes.

They shared their system with self-employed friends, realised that there was a market for it, and got to work improving their solution .In 2017, James and Claire officially launched Hnry; a service designed to automatically calculate, pay, and file taxes for sole traders.

Today, Hnry is New Zealand’s largest, and Australasia’s fastest-growing accounting service. We process billions of dollars worth of payments every year, handling around 1% of New Zealand’s tax revenue.

Best of all, we free up thousands of hours for clients to focus more on what they do best - their jobs. Hnry is on a mission to make self-employment simple, affordable, and accessible for anyone.

long_description:
Christmas Fantasia

Saturday 5 December, 7pm

Wellington Cathedral of St Paul, 2 Hill Street, Thorndon


General admission $35 (early bird price $30 until midnight 29 Nov)

Concession $30 (early bird concession price $27 until midnight 29 Nov)

School-aged children free


Nota Bene presents: Christmas Fantasia

From centuries-old texts to traditional carols given new musical life, this concert explores the many ways composers across different eras and cultures have interpreted the Christmas story.

Our programme brings together music from England to Appalachia, with works by Vaughan Williams, Warlock, Dalglish and Ešenvalds. The music ranges from reflective settings and rich harmonies to folk-inspired carols and familiar Christmas melodies.

Vaughan Williams’ Fantasia on Christmas Carols weaves together traditional English carol melodies, some emerging in the choir and others in the accompaniment. In contrast, Malcolm Dalglish’s Star in the East sets three Appalachian Christmas songs for choir and harp, drawing on a different folk tradition.

Joined by baritone Joe Haddow, harpist Michelle Velvin and organist Rachel Malcolm-Swindells, Nota Bene presents a programme that moves between familiar carols and less familiar musical settings.

And what better way to finish than by singing some favourite Christmas carols together? As is our tradition, we hope you’ll stay and join us for refreshments after the concert.

Rachel Malcolm-Swindells - Organ

Michelle Velvin - Harp

Joe Haddow - Baritone

long_description:
This course is aimed at all health care professionals with an interest in Palliative Care bring. The first day brings learnings from this year's Advanced Course in Pain and Symptom Management which Mary runs in Oxford. On the second day Mary will share her knowledge from being National Clinical Lead for the UK audit of Care at the End of Life. This is both findings from the recent audit, but also practical ways to bring audit into palliative care settings.

Biography:

Dr Mary Miller

Consultant in Palliative Medicine, Sobell House, Honorary Senior Clinical Lecturer in Palliative Medicine, University of Oxford, Director OxCERPC (Oxford Centre for education and research in palliative care), national clinical lead for the National Audit of Care at the End of Life.

Mary qualified from University College Cork, Ireland in 1988. She trained and worked in palliative medicine in Ireland, Sweden and the UK before starting as a consultant in palliative medicine in Oxford in 1998. 

Mary has a strong interest in education; she completed a Diploma in Learning and Teaching at Oxford University in 2005, was Training Programme Director and Regional Specialty Advisor (2002 – 2008) and led the Oxford Advanced Courses in Pain and Symptom Management from 2005. Since the inception of OxCERPC in 2017, Mary and the team are focusing on building an exciting portfolio of courses, building research readiness and reaching out to practitioners across the globe.

name: Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride
venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Described by the 2026 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate panel as "without a doubt one of New Zealand's most important living writers", internationally bestselling author Catherine Chidgey returns to Verb to discuss her tenth enthralling novel. The Starving Bride is an urgent and searing story set in near-future England.


Dumped by her boyfriend, fired from her job and estranged from her parents, Hazel Whitlock signs up for a sideshow act in Blackpool. The seaside resort has revived all the cancelled old favourites and she will be the Starving Bride. On display in the iconic Blackpool Tower, with a ravenous lion prowling the enclosure, Hazel must lie in silence while strangers view her body.

Join Catherine and Kate Camp for a special one-night event as they discuss the many layers of The Starving Bride, writing female experiences and the questions the book raises about spectacle, desire, survival and society's obsession with beauty.

Unity Books will be at the event bookselling and Catherine will be book signing.

Cover artwork by Max Thompson. Cover design by Todd Atticus. Author photo by Ebony Lamb.

Catherine Chidgey’s novels have been published to international acclaim. Her first, In a Fishbone Church, won Best First Book at the New Zealand Book Awards and at the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize (South East Asia and South Pacific). In the UK it won the Betty Trask Award and was longlisted for the Orange Prize.

Her second, Golden Deeds, was a Notable Book of the Year in the New York Times Book Review and a Best Book in the LA Times. Catherine has won the Prize in Modern Letters, the Katherine Mansfield Award, the Katherine Mansfield Fellowship, the Janet Frame Fiction Prize, and, for her 2016 novel The Wish Child, the Acorn Foundation Fiction Prize.

Her 2020 novel, Remote Sympathy, was shortlisted for the DUBLIN Literary Award and the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction, and was longlisted for the Women’s Prize for Fiction. The Axeman’s Carnival (2022) won the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction. Catherine's two most recent novels are the critically acclaimed Pet (2023) and The Book of Guilt (2025), also published by John Murray.

Catherine lectures in Creative Writing at the University of Waikato.

Kate Camp is the author of many collections of poems, including The Mirror of Simple Annihilated Souls (winner of the 2011 NZ Post Book Award for Poetry) and How to Be Happy Though Human: New and Selected Poems (2020), and a collection of essays, You Probably Think This Song Is About You (2022). Her most recent book is Makeshift Seasons (2025), a new collection of poetry. Kate was born in 1972 and lives in Wellington.

id: LinerGame Industry Open Workshop - Wellington, New Zealand - June 2027-shed 39/2 Fryatt Quay, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: LinerGame Industry Open Workshop - Wellington, New Zealand - June 2027
venue: shed 39/2 Fryatt Quay, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Hosted by CentrePort

We're grateful to CentrePort for hosting LinerGame in Wellington, bringing the workshop right to the waterfront of the capital's port.

The workshop is open to everyone across New Zealand's supply chain: shipping lines, forwarders, customs brokers, importers and exporters, ports and transport operators. If you have ever wanted to see how a liner service is really run, this is the day.

Wednesday 16 June 2027 · 10:00 am – 4:30 pm · CentrePort Wellington, Fryatt Quay, Pipitea, Wellington

Early Bird Special: NZD 299 per person until 31 March 2027 (standard price NZD 385). Places are limited.

About the LinerGame

The LinerGame is a hands-on simulation of running a container shipping service. Working in teams, you take on the roles inside a shipping line: taking bookings, planning vessel stowage, managing terminal operations and balancing revenue against cost, while the market throws real-world disruption at you.

It works equally well for people new to the industry and for seasoned professionals, because every decision has a visible consequence for the customer, the vessel and the bottom line.

Key features include:

Booking Uptake: Manage dynamic booking requests while balancing capacity constraints and customer expectations.

Vessel Stowage: Plan and optimise vessel space, considering cargo types, weight distribution, and voyage schedules.

Terminal Operations: Coordinate port activities, manage container flows, and ensure efficient cargo handling.

For a closer look at the LinerGame experience, watch the highlight video below.

Skip embedded content
What you'll take away

The carrier's view. See how a shipping line weighs bookings, capacity, schedules and cost, and why decisions that look odd from the outside make sense from the inside.

Better negotiations and decisions. Bring that understanding back to your own contracts, bookings and planning conversations with carriers, forwarders and customers.

A wider network. Spend a day working alongside peers from across New Zealand's supply chain.

Your facilitator

Peter Creeden, Strategic Advisor and LinerGame Partner

Peter spent 22 years at Hamburg Süd, rising to Managing Director Oceania. He now advises ports, shipping lines and logistics providers, and teaches at the University of Sydney and the Australian Maritime College. He brings that carrier-side experience into every session.

Why attend?

Supply chain decisions are often made without a clear view of what the other side is dealing with. The LinerGame closes that gap in a single day, in a risk-free setting where mistakes are part of the learning. By attending, you will:

Understand Complex Operations: Experience the decision-making process of running a liner shipping service, covering end-to-end operations.

Enhance Your Skills: Improve your teamwork, strategic thinking, and revenue management capabilities in a fast-paced, risk-free environment.

Navigate Real-World Scenarios: Encounter challenges like port strikes, equipment shortages, weather disruptions, and overlapping booking regions, gaining critical insights into effective problem-solving.

Network with Industry Peers: Connect with like-minded professionals in a collaborative setting, exchange ideas, and explore new opportunities within the shipping and logistics sector.

Who should attend?

This workshop is ideal for:

Logistics & Supply Chain Professionals: Individuals involved in operations, planning, and management.

Importers & Exporters: Professionals managing supply chain activities and interested in gaining a broader understanding of liner shipping dynamics.

Freight Forwarders & Shippers: Those seeking to enhance their service offerings by understanding carrier operations better.

Port & Terminal Operators: Professionals responsible for terminal management and coordination.

Shipping Lines & Carriers: Executives and teams who want to refine their strategies and processes.

Bring your team

The day works best when people from different parts of a business play side by side. We encourage companies to send two or three people across functions, such as sales, customer service, operations and procurement, so the insights travel back into the office.

Trusted across the industry

Since 2014, more than 3,000 participants from over 30 countries have taken part in over 150 LinerGame sessions, from shipping line leadership teams to port executives, forwarders and cargo owners. Organisations that have played include Kotahi, Port of Melbourne, MSC, Kuehne+Nagel and RHI Magnesita.

name: Welly Biotech ‘n’ Beers - 27 November
venue: 7 Dixon Street, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
The final instalment of BioTech N Beers: Speaker Series 2026 is here!

Our final speaker of the year is Mike Hartevelt, a biotechnology and pharmaceutical leader who has recently returned to Wellington after seven years in the US, where he led global oncology policy and government affairs at MSD.

Mike will share insights and experiences from his career spanning scientific research, commercialisation, market access and global pharmaceutical policy, including what it takes to bring innovative medicines to patients and navigate the international pharmaceutical landscape.

Kindly hosted by Creative HQ and generously sponsored by Wellington UniVentures, come along for a yarn, some war stories, and drinks and kai.

Wellington UniVentures:

Building on our purpose to lift lives everywhere with knowledge, Wellington UniVentures works with our University innovators to shape their research into initiatives that create impact. We do this by building powerful teams, connecting respected specialists and academics with industry, governments and educators - matching ideas with opportunities, people with people, knowledge with needs. And while it’s knowledge we share, it’s people who make the difference – our team, innovators and experts, those we partner with and the people whose lives we help change. Everyone here has a genuine desire to help people develop – it starts in Wellington and we take it to the world.

 

Creative HQ:

Creative HQ is a global innovation hub, based in New Zealand, that provides programmes for entrepreneurship and public sector innovation. Creative HQ creates change for governments and startups through innovation training, structured acceleration programmes and bespoke support. Creative HQ, Wellington’s innovation hub, operates throughout New Zealand and internationally across the Asia-Pacific region with significant work experience in the Philippines, Singapore, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Japan, Hong Kong, India and Australia. They look to build confidence, capability and connectedness throughout their ecosystem while looking to inspire and support the growth of individuals and businesses through the use of design thinking methodologies. This enables the delivery of innovative solutions to their customers.

We look forward to joining you! 

Date: Friday, 27 November

Time: 4.30PM - 6.30PM

Location: Creative HQ, 7 Dixon Street, Wellington 6011 

Event Type: In person

Cost: Free for members & for non-members

Supported by

id: Shaping streets that put people first-139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Shaping streets that put people first
venue: 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Streets are the largest network of public space in our cities, yet for decades we’ve designed them mainly to move and store cars. Around the world, that’s changing fast. From Bogotá to Paris, cities are reimagining their streets as places to walk, play, meet, shop and breathe.

Drawing on lessons from the Global Street Design Guide and Designing Streets for Kids, this talk shares inspiring stories and striking before-and-after transformations from cities across the globe. It’s a celebration of what’s possible when we design streets for people, and an invitation to imagine what our own streets could become.

id: Women of Pōneke November 2026 Event-70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Women of Pōneke November 2026 Event
venue: 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Women of Pōneke : Together by Design - The Next Chapter

26 November |5pm -7.30pm | Te Ahumairangi Foyer

National Library 70 Molesworth St

Women of Pōneke exists to elevate women in our city, and it starts with connection. We are ambitious about where that can go, and we are here to serve the women who make it what it is.

On Thursday 26 November, we are bringing everyone together for an evening that is Together by Design.

First and foremost, this is a night out: lively, warm and relaxed. Come with a crowd, or come on your own and leave having met someone new. Expect laughter, easy conversation and time to unwind in a welcoming space, the Te Ahumairangi Foyer at the National Library on Molesworth Street in Thorndon.

The food will be amazing and you will leave well nourished. Everybody Eats, the social enterprise that looked after us in September, is providing the platters, and Luna Estate will be pouring the wine. We are paying Everybody Eats the full value of the catering, so every ticket helps a social enterprise thrive and puts our community’s support to work close to home.

The evening also opens a conversation about what comes next. We have some big ideas, and we reckon you will too. Women of Pōneke is working with Kathryn Robinson and Celine Yockney from Verian, who have generously contributed their research and engagement expertise to help us design the event and make sense of what we hear from you.

We will talk it through over a glass of bubbles or juice. We will share a little of our thinking, we want to hear yours, and your answers will shape what we build.

A ticket gets you good food, warm company and a seat at the table for what comes next. All are welcome, so bring a colleague, invite someone whose company you enjoy and come ready to have fun. We cannot wait to see you there.

We know things are busy in the run to the end of the year, so here are four reasons to come:

Nourishing kai and wine: platters from Everybody Eats, with Luna Estate pouring.

Warm company: familiar faces and new ones, in an evening built for connecting and unwinding.

Your ticket makes a difference: the full catering value supports a social enterprise.

A seat at the table: big ideas for what comes next, shaped by you.

So grab your ticket now and share with at least one amazing woman (and/or ally) in your life.

To cover our costs, we are charging for this event. We know that things are tough at the moment for many, so if this is a barrier for you to attend, please contact us and we will do everything to support you to attend. 

Help a woman in need

If you wish to support someone else who may have a financial barrier, please buy one of the "Buy-One, Give-One" tickets, so we can support more of the amazing women of Pōneke to attend.

Get in quick!

Tickets for previous events have sold out fast. For this event we are capped at 250 people attending and we will be updating our social media channels on the progress of the ticket sales, so get your tickets quick.  

Accessibility
The Te Ahumairangi Foyer, National Library is fully accessible. If you are not able to use the steps on Molesworth Street, you will be able to access the venue via the lift off Aitken Street. There will be staff at the door to be able to support and guide you to the venue space.

A bit about us 

Me.We.Pōneke is our signature quarterly event designed to inspire, connect and raise the voices of our wonderful community of Wellington women, and people who identify as women. 

We believe that magic happens when women come together. We’ve seen it. We’ve felt it. And we want to create more of it with regular events that are open, welcoming, supportive and empowering for the women of Wellington.

Come along, bring a friend and join us as we continue to raise the voices of Wellington women and invite you all to be part of Me We Pōneke.

We are so grateful to all of our supporters, especially Steph and the team at Inside Recruitment.

You can join our mailing list from website, thanks to our amazing partner Springload. Check it out here and make sure you sign up to our mailing list: https://www.womenofponeke.org....

We are also on Insta! Follow us here: https://www.instagram.com/wome…

Immerse yourself in a breathtaking 3-hour cinematic journey into the world’s most spectacular marine environments. The Ocean Film Festival World Tour brings together an extraordinary collection of short films celebrating the beauty, power and wonder of our oceans.

From crystal-clear tropical reefs and wild coastlines to towering waves and the depths of the open ocean, these beautifully crafted films showcase the ocean from every perspective. Meet the passionate divers, fearless surfers, dedicated ocean advocates, ocean explorers and marine scientists whose lives are shaped by their connection to the sea.

Featuring spectacular underwater cinematography, heart-stopping ocean adventures and intimate stories of the people who dedicate their lives to exploring and protecting our oceans, every film offers a fresh perspective on the world beneath the waves.

Along the way, encounter remarkable marine creatures, discover remote underwater environments and experience the thrill of ocean adventure through the eyes of those who know it best.

The Ocean Film Festival World Tour is a celebration of our oceans in all their beauty, diversity and power. Inspiring, entertaining and thought-provoking, it’s an unforgettable experience that will leave you with a deeper appreciation for the incredible marine environments that connect us all.

The Ocean Film Festival is exempt from Classification, but all swearing has been beeped out.

Recommended age 10+

id: Hybrid Warfare Beyond the Battlefield: Small-State Resilience and Lessons from Estonia-55 Lambton Quay, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Hybrid Warfare Beyond the Battlefield: Small-State Resilience and Lessons from Estonia
venue: 55 Lambton Quay, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Drawing on Estonia’s experience from the 2007 cyberattacks to more recent acts of sabotage, airspace violations and other forms of hostile activity, this presentation examines how hybrid threats challenge the security and resilience of small states. It explores how Russia combines military intimidation, cyber operations, sabotage and information warfare to undermine public confidence, exploit societal vulnerabilities and incite political divisions.  The presentation highlights how these actions are part of Russia’s broader confrontation with Western democracies and an extension of its war against Ukraine beyond the battlefield. Estonia’s experience offers lessons on strengthening national resilience, deterring hostile actions and defending the principles underpinning the international order.  

Refreshments will be provided at the event.

long_description:
Jazz and Beyond for students 19 and under

December 14–17, 2026

Coordinated by Chris Beernink, Dave Wilson, Daniel Hayles, Andrew Faleatua, Lance Philip. Proudly supported by the Tauranga Jazz Society.

Take it to the next level as a player or vocalist at the Jazz and Beyond Workshops! Young musicians from across Aotearoa come together to dive into jazz and connected styles, working closely with some of the country’s leading performers and educators. In a friendly, inclusive environment, you’ll grow your skills, make new musical connections, and learn alongside other students your age from all around the motu.

Here’s what’s in store:

small group ensembles led by professional musicians

developing improvisation skills in supportive settings

an introduction to music production

listening sessions that expand your skills

inclusive jam sessions where all are welcome

ensemble performances at the end of week concert

And more!

If you're 19 or under with at least a year of experience on your instrument or in vocal training, you’re welcome to join. Choose from trumpet, trombone, saxophone, clarinet, flute, bass, piano, guitar, drums, vibraphone, or voice.

The workshops are held at the New Zealand School of Music–Te Kōkī at Te Herenga Waka-Victoria University of Wellington. Follow the Jazz and Beyond Workshops on Instagram or Facebook for the latest updates. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com with any questions.

Schedule

The workshops run 9:00am-4:30pm Monday through Thursday, with evening activities including concerts and our inclusive jam sessions Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Students perform in a closing concert on Thursday afternoon.

Accommodation

Students arrange their own accommodation. Often students from outside Wellington stay together in groups with a parent chaperone. Options for housing near Victoria University of Wellington include backpacker hostels and hotels. If you have a group of 15 or more, University Student Housing may be an option. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com if you'd like to pursue this option.

Meals

Lunch for the four days is available for purchase at many convenient locations on campus, or students may bring their own lunch.

Equipment

Provided equipment includes drum kits, guitar and bass amps, pianos/keyboards, microphones and PAs for vocalists.

All brass and wind players should bring their own instruments.

Drummers: you are required to bring your own cymbals, sticks, and hi-hat clutch.

Guitarists and bass players: you are required to bring your own instruments as well as cables (leads).

Preparation

All students with one year of experience on an instrument or in vocal training have the skills required to participate, so no musical preparation is required. On the first day, students will play a very short audition to be placed in an appropriate ensemble. Guidelines for this short audition will be sent to all registered participants in advance of the workshops.

Cost

Early bird price: $325 - register before 19th October

Standard price $350 - on or after 19th October

Registration is open to all until all spots are filled.

We are dedicated to ensuring all students can participate in the workshops without financial constraints. If the cost poses a barrier, please email us at jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com and we will find a solution to facilitate your participation!

id: MATRESCENCE Development Showing-12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, Nueva Zelanda-Humanitix
name: MATRESCENCE Development Showing
venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, Nueva Zelanda
long_description:
MATRESCENCE

A development showing at Hannah Playhouse

A solo show about the collision of early motherhood, migration and art making.

A mother tries to care for her baby. An artist tries to make a show.

MATRESCENCE follows Ella (“she” in Spanish), a migrant theatremaker and new mother trying to remain creatively alive while navigating the demands, exhaustion and disorientation of early motherhood.

Part testimonial, part creative crisis and part documentary, MATRESCENCE is an anti-biography that moves between Ella’s intimate experience of postpartum life and her attempt to make theatre from inside it. She reaches out to other migrant mothers and theatremakers, searching for answers about care, identity, creativity and belonging. But the more stories she gathers, the less this seems to be a story about one woman.

Join us for a special development showing of MATRESCENCE at Hannah Playhouse, a glimpse into the making of this new documentary theatre work. This is an opportunity to experience the work in progress and be part of its creative journey.

Following the showing, we invite you to stay for an informal Q&A - audience conversation. We would love to hear your thoughts, reflections and responses to the work, while opening up a wider conversation about postpartum, care work, and the complexities of motherhood, particularly when home, family and support networks are far away.

The work is informed by research into matrescence, migration and caregiving, interviews, as well as anonymous testimonies from migrant mothers living in Aotearoa.

Please note: This is a work in development showing, not a finished production. Your presence, thoughts and feedback are warmly welcomed and will contribute to the ongoing development of MATRESCENCE.

CREATIVE TEAM

Created and performed by Romina Meneses

Directed by Mel Dodge

Production Managment: Jessie Rochford-Barber

Lights and AV design: Janis Cheng

Sound Design: Alex Quinn

Set and Costume Design: Miho Aragane

Photo by Charlie Jewell

long_description:
🤖 AI, MARK MY WORDS!

Write it. Test the AI. Trust your judgement.

Can AI really improve your writing? Or does it sometimes get things wrong?

Join Viet Hub NZ for a FREE, fun and interactive writing workshop where YOU get to challenge AI, spot its mistakes and discover how to become a more confident writer.

Whether you're writing an email to your teacher, applying for a job, preparing an essay or studying for IELTS, this workshop is for you!

🌟 Meet your workshop leader – Kai.

We're excited to have Kai (Anh Khoa Dang), one of Viet Hub NZ's passionate young volunteers, leading this workshop.

At Viet Hub NZ, we believe young people have incredible ideas and deserve opportunities to bring them to life.

Kai has already been supporting learners through our IELTS Writing sessions. Now he's taking the next step – designing and leading his own workshop to help others develop practical writing skills.

Young minds. Bold ideas. The courage to try something new!

Come along, learn something useful and support a young community leader!

✍️ What will you do?

This isn't a workshop where you just sit and listen. You'll be writing, experimenting, discussing and putting AI to the test!

Hey → Dear! Turn a casual text message into a professional email. Can you write a better version than AI?

Spot the 8 writing traps! Discover common mistakes in tone, vocabulary and structure.

Choose your writing challenge! Write an email, job application paragraph or short essay.

Let AI mark your words! Ask AI to review your writing and see what it notices.

Human vs AI! Compare AI's feedback with another participant's. Who catches more mistakes?

You'll also receive practical take-home resources to continue improving your writing.

🎯 Who should join?

This workshop is particularly useful for:

School and university students

IELTS and English-language learners

Jobseekers preparing applications

Anyone who wants to write clearer, more professional emails

Curious minds who want to learn how to use AI responsibly

No advanced writing or AI experience required!

The workshop is delivered in English, with Vietnamese-language support available where needed.

📅 Event details

Date: Saturday 28 November 2026

Time: 1:00–3:00 PM

Location: Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub

Address: 203 Willis Street, Te Aro, Wellington

Cost: FREE

Spaces: Limited to 25 registrations

📱 What to bring

A fully charged smartphone with internet access

A free AI chatbot app, if you already have one

Your curiosity and willingness to try something new!

Don't have an AI app? No worries! You can follow the live demonstrations or work with a partner.

💛 Why we're doing this

At Viet Hub NZ, we want to create more opportunities for young people to lead, share their knowledge and contribute to their communities.

This workshop is about more than writing. It's about encouraging independent thinking, building confidence and showing that technology works best when we remain curious and critical.

AI can suggest the words. But you decide what they mean.

🎟️ Reserve your FREE place today.

Organised by Viet Hub NZ, with venue support from Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub.

Please note: This is a practical learning workshop, not a formal IELTS assessment or band-scoring session.

long_description:
Women of Pōneke : Together by Design - The Next Chapter

26 November |5pm -7.30pm | Te Ahumairangi Foyer

National Library 70 Molesworth St

Women of Pōneke exists to elevate women in our city, and it starts with connection. We are ambitious about where that can go, and we are here to serve the women who make it what it is.

On Thursday 26 November, we are bringing everyone together for an evening that is Together by Design.

First and foremost, this is a night out: lively, warm and relaxed. Come with a crowd, or come on your own and leave having met someone new. Expect laughter, easy conversation and time to unwind in a welcoming space, the Te Ahumairangi Foyer at the National Library on Molesworth Street in Thorndon.

The food will be amazing and you will leave well nourished. Everybody Eats, the social enterprise that looked after us in September, is providing the platters, and Luna Estate will be pouring the wine. We are paying Everybody Eats the full value of the catering, so every ticket helps a social enterprise thrive and puts our community’s support to work close to home.

The evening also opens a conversation about what comes next. We have some big ideas, and we reckon you will too. Women of Pōneke is working with Kathryn Robinson and Celine Yockney from Verian, who have generously contributed their research and engagement expertise to help us design the event and make sense of what we hear from you.

We will talk it through over a glass of bubbles or juice. We will share a little of our thinking, we want to hear yours, and your answers will shape what we build.

A ticket gets you good food, warm company and a seat at the table for what comes next. All are welcome, so bring a colleague, invite someone whose company you enjoy and come ready to have fun. We cannot wait to see you there.

We know things are busy in the run to the end of the year, so here are four reasons to come:

Nourishing kai and wine: platters from Everybody Eats, with Luna Estate pouring.

Warm company: familiar faces and new ones, in an evening built for connecting and unwinding.

Your ticket makes a difference: the full catering value supports a social enterprise.

A seat at the table: big ideas for what comes next, shaped by you.

So grab your ticket now and share with at least one amazing woman (and/or ally) in your life.

To cover our costs, we are charging for this event. We know that things are tough at the moment for many, so if this is a barrier for you to attend, please contact us and we will do everything to support you to attend. 

Help a woman in need

If you wish to support someone else who may have a financial barrier, please buy one of the "Buy-One, Give-One" tickets, so we can support more of the amazing women of Pōneke to attend.

Get in quick!

Tickets for previous events have sold out fast. For this event we are capped at 250 people attending and we will be updating our social media channels on the progress of the ticket sales, so get your tickets quick.  

Accessibility
The Te Ahumairangi Foyer, National Library is fully accessible. If you are not able to use the steps on Molesworth Street, you will be able to access the venue via the lift off Aitken Street. There will be staff at the door to be able to support and guide you to the venue space.

A bit about us 

Me.We.Pōneke is our signature quarterly event designed to inspire, connect and raise the voices of our wonderful community of Wellington women, and people who identify as women. 

We believe that magic happens when women come together. We’ve seen it. We’ve felt it. And we want to create more of it with regular events that are open, welcoming, supportive and empowering for the women of Wellington.

Come along, bring a friend and join us as we continue to raise the voices of Wellington women and invite you all to be part of Me We Pōneke.

We are so grateful to all of our supporters, especially Steph and the team at Inside Recruitment.

You can join our mailing list from website, thanks to our amazing partner Springload. Check it out here and make sure you sign up to our mailing list: https://www.womenofponeke.org....

We are also on Insta! Follow us here: https://www.instagram.com/wome…

venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Tales from Nowhereland: Sephirot, by Ted Mills, is presented as part of his PhD research, in association with Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts at Massey University.

Bringing together surrealism, occult practices, storytelling and speculative ideas about life beyond late-stage capitalism, the work explores the possibility of returning to theatre's magical and ritualistic origins.

Across ten interconnected stories, video projections, hypnotic soundscapes and lighting, a surreal landscape emerges - shaped by dreams and divination, with the help of Simon Ward and Alan Wells.

Location: Massey University, Block 1, Te Kōhure, Pukeahu Mount Cook, Wellington.

Tickets: $12.00 general public, $5.00 discounted tickets for Massey students and staff

id: Native Fungi for Food Resilience: Beginners Workshop at Kaicycle, Newtown-5 Hospital Road, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Native Fungi for Food Resilience: Beginners Workshop at Kaicycle, Newtown
venue: 5 Hospital Road, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Fungi for food security 🍄

Mushrooms are one of the fastest ways to grow nutritious food at home. In this hands-on workshop, Mihau and Valetta of Matariki Mushrooms show you simple, permaculture-inspired, low-tech methods for turning everyday waste like straw, sawdust and garden offcuts into high-quality, protein-rich food in just a few weeks.

What you'll learn

Native fungi of Aotearoa: an introduction to our native species, their traditional uses and their role in our ecosystems

Ways to grow: an overview of different growing methods, from low-tech to more advanced, and which suit growing at home

Hands-on: make your own grow kit with gourmet native oyster mushrooms

Expanding your own spawn: learn how to multiply your spawn, which makes growing mushrooms at home much more affordable, almost free

What you'll take home

Your own grow kit and spawn, ready for a first harvest in about 4 weeks

The know-how to keep producing mushrooms at home for years to come

Good to know

When: Saturday 16 January 2027, 1–5pm

Where: Kaicycle Urban Farm, 5 Hospital Road, Newtown, Wellington (an outdoor farm setting, so dress for the weather)

Included: all materials, an introduction to fungi ecology and a hands-on practical session

Please bring: two clean 2L ice-cream containers with lids, and a plate to share for afternoon tea (shared kai)

Early bird: $90 until 20 December, then $100

Bookings essential: spaces are limited, please book online

Gift idea: a ticket makes a great Christmas present

Afterpay available: pay in 4 interest-free instalments

Keep growing: Advanced workshop

Ready for the next step? Join our Advanced · Logs & Liquid Culture workshop on Saturday 30 January: grow native shiitake on logs, make dowel spawn and liquid culture, and take home your own inoculated log and a syringe of pekepeke-kiore (a native cousin of lion's mane). Book both workshops and get a free copy of our book "Family of Forest and Fungi - He Tukutuku Toiora."

id: Te Whiri Whītau 2026: Fibre Futures - Connection, Reflection and Potential-Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Te Whiri Whītau 2026: Fibre Futures - Connection, Reflection and Potential
venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Come and join Te Whiri Whītau as we celebrate a year of learning, making, connecting and dreaming together.

We warmly invite you to join in conversation, connection and celebration as we reflect on the year that has been and share our aspirations for the future. This gathering is an opportunity to learn more about the work of Te Whiri Whītau, hear about current and emerging research, meet our researchers and collaborators, and explore opportunities for collaboration, partnership, creative practice and research.

Over the course of the event, we'll share research highlights, introduce our new visual identity, and open conversations about the role that fibres, textiles and materials can play in creating thriving communities, cultures, environments and economies.

Whether you are a researcher, practitioner, student, industry partner, community organisation or supporter of our work, we would love you to join us as we strengthen connections, celebrate achievements, and look ahead to what's possible together.

Light refreshments will be served.

id: Unity Book Club November 2026 | Exit Party-57 Willis Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Unity Book Club November 2026 | Exit Party
venue: 57 Willis Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Eden and Mrittika will be hosting our monthly book club to discuss some of the excellent recently released books.

In November we will be discussing Exit Party by Emily St John Mandel.

About the book:

Los Angeles, 2031: The first spring after the collapse of the United States, peacekeeping troops withdraw from the city, the Jacaranda trees blossom, and the curfew is finally lifted. Ari Waker and her roommate pass the gauntlet of bomb-sniffing dogs, the shanty towns, and the Red Cross tents as they walk across Silverlake to a party. The mood is ecstatic inside the apartment, people drink and dance, a woman wears a silver dress, pleated like tinfoil. And then: A shift. A bewildered twin, an uncanny doppelganger stumbles through the crowd and out into the night, and Kareem, the party’s host, vanishes into thin air.

As Ari Waker unravels the mystery of this inexplicable night, Emily St. John Mandel unfurls a story that takes us from a future America splintered by civil war to the seaside cliffs of Greece where weapons dealers hide in an elegant resort, and from the domed city of Paris to a colony on the moon. Exit Party is a novel about the price of safety, the perils of the surveillance state, a requiem for a world not unlike our own, and a breathtaking story of resilience in the face of cataclysmic change.


We have limited tickets available so grab one sooner rather then later and tell your friends and whānau.

Drinks and snacks provided. If you have any specific allergies, let us know and send an email.

If you have any further queries send us an email to wellington@unitybooks.co.nz and address it to Eden.

name: Unsung Heroes presents Cameron Bennett and Chris Priestley
venue: 118 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Unsung Heroes!

Cameron Bennett and Chris Priestley -with special guest Angela Fox- share songs, stories and a slideshow from NZ's distant past. Together, they bring to life the characters and stories of our past - the quirky and macabre - that shaped who we are today.

Chris Priestley is a singer, songwriter & NZ historian. He has recorded eight albums and his musical spans over 40 years. As a hospitality entrepreneur he was co-founder of Real Groovy Records & café/music venues Java Jive, Kerouacs, Atomic and Café One2One in Ponsonby.

Cameron Bennett is a storyteller, singer songwriter and plays guitar and lap steel guitar. Journalism is his day job - he currently produces a weekly tv current affairs programme and is director/writer of the ongoing NZ Land Wars documentaries. New Zealand colonial history is in his blood; from the Wairau Affray to the Western Front, his forebears have borne witness - miners, gamblers, union organisers, shopkeepers and servicemen.

Saturday Nov 28

Doors 7pm

Music 7:30pm

$20 ($15 unwaged)

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

We’ll see you there ☆

id: The Muppet Christmas Carol - booking-10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: The Muppet Christmas Carol - booking
venue: 10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
G

To celebrate the end of the year and the festive season Wellington Film Society is putting on a screening of The Muppet Christmas Carol. We'd love for families to come along to enjoy this film together. Tickets are free. Seats are unallocated, just enter the cinema on the day and find a seat. We start films on time and do not play trailers.

BOOKING DETAILS


First phase - Monday 9 November to Friday 20 November: Wellington Film Society member only booking (members can book up to 5 seats and can bring non-members guests).

Second phase from 20 November: public booking - anyone including non-members can book up to 5 seats directly.

We will make all seats bookable because we’re enabling members to bring guests and non-members to attend.

The point of opening this screening up to the public is to enable children to have a fun film experience so please act in this spirit. You can book up to five seats, but please don’t book more seats than you need is as many people can come as possible.

FILM DETAILS

There have been countless adaptations of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, but no other stars Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, Gonzo, and Rizzo the Rat! The Muppets put a hilarious and chaotic spin on the most iconic Christmas story in literature. The film is elevated by the central performance of the only human cast member, Michael Caine as miserly Ebenezer Scrooge, who delivers on the promise he made when he took on the role, "I'm going to play this movie like I'm working with the Royal Shakespeare Company. I will never wink, I will never do anything Muppety. I am going to play Scrooge as if it is an utterly dramatic role and there are no puppets around me.”

Directed by Brian Henson, son of Muppet creator Jim Henson, The Muppet Christmas Carol follows the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine) as he is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve, forcing him to confront the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future – and perhaps discover a little festive spirit along the way. Featuring a superb collection of songs by Paul Williams (Phantom of the Paradise) the film manages to balance genuine emotional heft with the anarchic silliness that makes the Muppets so enduringly wonderful.

More than thirty years on, The Muppet Christmas Carol has become regarded as one of the best and most beloved Christmas films. A film for children, adults, Muppet enthusiasts, and anyone who could do with a little boost towards the end of the year.

id: The Lone Prairie Brothers Play The Shed-46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: The Lone Prairie Brothers Play The Shed
venue: 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Originally from the wilds of the south west of the UK, Phil Lively-Masters is an experienced, dynamic and well travelled singer songwriter, who specialises in writing the sort of Sun Kissed West Coast Laurel Canyon Americana and Roots Rock that made Neil Young, Stephen Stills, the Byrds and 'Wildflowers' era Tom Petty famous. With a powerful, honey soaked voice that has won praise and support slots from the likes of legendary American country rock pioneers The Jayhawks, Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando, original outlaw cosmic cowboy Steve Young (writer of Seven Bridges Road), Neil Halstead (Slowdive, Mojave 3) and received critical praise for acoustic slots at festivals such as Glastonbury and Maverick in the UK. 

Now based in Napier, Hawke's Bay, Phil has 20 years worth of road worn original songs to pull on, covering all the Roots/ Americana elements, with a skilful blend of Country, Rock, Blues and Folk. Having recently been inspired by a sonmgwriting stint in East Nashville, Phil came back to NZ and teamed up with local Lead guitar Telecaster Master Neil Matcheson as a new Americana duo 'The Lone Prairie Brothers', they are currently in the process of short listing songs for a new self titled debut album and racking up live gigs and great reviews in 2026, weaving Phil's trusty Guild 12 and 6 string guitars with Neil's versatile and exciting Telecaster licks; airing brand new songs and including some choice tracks from Phil's previous critically acclaimed UK band CANYON RYDE, (and their album 'Free To Be'), ready to weave a sun kissed, melodic americana spell on any listener.

Reviews for the Canyon Ryde album...

UNCUT MAGAZINE: ‘A prime platter...perfect for those attuned to the soft driftwood sounds of Buffalo Springfield and Gram Parsons'

MOJO MAGAZINE: ‘An excellent and very mature sounding debut in ‘Free to Be’. Another fine example of a talented ‘under the radar’ outfit producing American inspired music as good as, if not better, than a lot of Americans on the same trip. Highly Recommended!’

Sony/Universal Music Historian Richard Havers: ‘Big Names in The Making’…The MAVERICK AMERICANA FESTIVAL... the opening act on the main stage was the intriguingly named Canyon Ryde, featuring the exquisite songs of Phil Lively-Masters. Imagine you’ve been stranded on a California hill farm circa 1969 and you get the vibe. Their music is just so damned catchy!’

MAVERICK MAGAZINE: ‘CANYON RYDE is the vehicle for singer-songwriter Phil Lively-Masters and his superb songs that are evocative of America’s West Coast countryish pop-rock of the late 1960s and early 1970s… with acclaimed players such as singer songwriter Peter Bruntnell and Gary Louris… It is a gorgeous listening experience, especially on the captivating ‘Marine Drive’.

AMERICANA UK: ‘’Subtle and dreamy country boasting a host of Americana luminaries... ‘Free to Be’ is a great country record that is subtle in its approach, gentle in its intentions"

id: Hybrid Warfare Beyond the Battlefield: Small-State Resilience and Lessons from Estonia-55 Lambton Quay, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Hybrid Warfare Beyond the Battlefield: Small-State Resilience and Lessons from Estonia
venue: 55 Lambton Quay, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Drawing on Estonia’s experience from the 2007 cyberattacks to more recent acts of sabotage, airspace violations and other forms of hostile activity, this presentation examines how hybrid threats challenge the security and resilience of small states. It explores how Russia combines military intimidation, cyber operations, sabotage and information warfare to undermine public confidence, exploit societal vulnerabilities and incite political divisions.  The presentation highlights how these actions are part of Russia’s broader confrontation with Western democracies and an extension of its war against Ukraine beyond the battlefield. Estonia’s experience offers lessons on strengthening national resilience, deterring hostile actions and defending the principles underpinning the international order.  

Refreshments will be provided at the event.

id: Shaping streets that put people first-139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Shaping streets that put people first
venue: 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Streets are the largest network of public space in our cities, yet for decades we’ve designed them mainly to move and store cars. Around the world, that’s changing fast. From Bogotá to Paris, cities are reimagining their streets as places to walk, play, meet, shop and breathe.

Drawing on lessons from the Global Street Design Guide and Designing Streets for Kids, this talk shares inspiring stories and striking before-and-after transformations from cities across the globe. It’s a celebration of what’s possible when we design streets for people, and an invitation to imagine what our own streets could become.

long_description:
The final instalment of BioTech N Beers: Speaker Series 2026 is here!

Our final speaker of the year is Mike Hartevelt, a biotechnology and pharmaceutical leader who has recently returned to Wellington after seven years in the US, where he led global oncology policy and government affairs at MSD.

Mike will share insights and experiences from his career spanning scientific research, commercialisation, market access and global pharmaceutical policy, including what it takes to bring innovative medicines to patients and navigate the international pharmaceutical landscape.

Kindly hosted by Creative HQ and generously sponsored by Wellington UniVentures, come along for a yarn, some war stories, and drinks and kai.

Wellington UniVentures:

Building on our purpose to lift lives everywhere with knowledge, Wellington UniVentures works with our University innovators to shape their research into initiatives that create impact. We do this by building powerful teams, connecting respected specialists and academics with industry, governments and educators - matching ideas with opportunities, people with people, knowledge with needs. And while it’s knowledge we share, it’s people who make the difference – our team, innovators and experts, those we partner with and the people whose lives we help change. Everyone here has a genuine desire to help people develop – it starts in Wellington and we take it to the world.

 

Creative HQ:

Creative HQ is a global innovation hub, based in New Zealand, that provides programmes for entrepreneurship and public sector innovation. Creative HQ creates change for governments and startups through innovation training, structured acceleration programmes and bespoke support. Creative HQ, Wellington’s innovation hub, operates throughout New Zealand and internationally across the Asia-Pacific region with significant work experience in the Philippines, Singapore, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Japan, Hong Kong, India and Australia. They look to build confidence, capability and connectedness throughout their ecosystem while looking to inspire and support the growth of individuals and businesses through the use of design thinking methodologies. This enables the delivery of innovative solutions to their customers.

We look forward to joining you!
